title: Some English Vowels Change Meaning
subtitle: Why English words sound the same to Spanish speakers — and how to fix it
description: Spanish has five clear vowels, but English has many more. Small vowel differences change meaning and affect listening and speaking scores at the Citizenship level.

categories.title: Short vs Long “i” Sounds (ship / sheep)
categories.description: English has two different "i" sounds ("i" and "ee"). Spanish has only one. This difference often causes listening and pronunciation mistakes.

sentences.sentence: Leave the key on the table.

categories.title: “Cup” vs “Cap” Sounds
categories.description: Spanish speakers often hear both sounds as "a", but in English these vowels are very different and change meaning.

sentences.sentence: I bought a cup of coffee.
He is wearing a red cap.
Put the bag under the table.

categories.title: “Full” vs “Fool” Sounds
categories.description: English uses both vowel quality and length. Spanish does not clearly separate these two sounds.
